## A useful definition does three things {#l1-recap }

1. Names the variable: $X$, $T$, $H$, …
2. States exactly what it represents, including units where needed.
3. Identifies its possible values well enough to classify it.


::: {.takeaway}
The meaning of $X$ stays fixed; its observed value depends on the random outcome.
:::

::: notes
Revisit the success criteria: “I can explain what a random variable represents and whether it is discrete or continuous.” Ask a student to define X for the four-coin experiment and justify why it is discrete. Contrast it with the fixed pen price. Remind students that “discrete” does not mean “integer”. Exit prompt: Give a discrete variable with non-integer values, then a continuous variable that is recorded to limited precision.
:::
